paper_title: A Bounded Parallel Intersection Type System
statement: Further work. Determining the precise complexity of inhabitation in the setting of system R remains an open and challenging problem. Addressing it would require resolving subtle combinatorial issues that arise from the interplay of bounded resources and vector-based type structures, making this a promising direction for future research.
context: An earlier system [7] imposes a similar dimensional restriction. We therefore provided a detailed comparison highlighting both conceptual similarities and key differences in expressiveness and technical treatment, throughout which demonstrating that system R offers a simpler and strictly more comprehensive framework that is easier to use in practice. Further work. Determining the precise complexity of inhabitation in the setting of system R remains an open and challenging problem. Addressing it would require resolving subtle combinatorial issues that arise from the interplay of bounded resources and vector-based type structures, making this a promising direction for future research. Another important avenue of investigation concerns type inference for system R. Since the system incorporates features of both set and multiset interpretations of types, it is not immediately clear whether the typability problem falls into NP or PSPACE, as established for related systems by Dudenhefner and Rehof [8]. Studying this question could provide deeper insight into the algorithmic behavior of the system. Similarly to system Rel of de Carvalho [6, Definition 4.1], it is interesting whether binary relations in system R can be related to term evaluation by means of a Krivine machine. As the system λCIL by Wells et al. [23] was also developed in the context of type inference problems, it would be interesting to compare it with the current system on the technical level. As the system Rel of de Carvalho uses relations in its models, it is interesting to see how the binary relations in the current system R fit into this kind of denotational semantics.

paper_title: A Bounded Parallel Intersection Type System
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 2
statement: In this paper we introduce and study a system (denoted system R1 ) with bounded parallel intersection providing a strict generalization of the multiset dimensional system [7], extending (and deepening the analysis of) decidable inhabitation under dimensional bound. Intuitively, system R occupies a position between the set-theoretic and the multiset dimensional systems of [7], employing a combination of intersection types represented as vectors of types (which are non-idempotent) and as sets of types (which are idempotent). A technical novelty of the system is the use of relations specifying type vector transformations that, intuitively, capture information flow between types in a derivation, and which mediate between vectors of types and sets of types. Dimensionality in this system is measured by the maximal length of vectors of sets of types that can be used to type a variable. Our main technical result is that inhabitation in bounded dimension is decidable in 2-EXPTIME, and for each fixed dimension, inhabitation is decidable in EXPTIME. We have corresponding lower bounds of EXPSPACE and PSPACE, respectively, and leave open the problem of closing the gaps.
context: A notion of dimensional bound was introduced by some of the present authors [7] for intersection type derivations. Intuitively, dimension measures the maximal cumulative width (number of components) of intersection types introduced for subterms in a derivation. Dimension can be measured in two ways, depending on whether width is measured over sets of types or multisets of types. The former corresponds to the standard, idempotent treatment of intersection types, the latter corresponds to a non-idempotent treatment. Relative to each measurement system, we considered inhabitation under dimensional bound: given a type and a dimensional bound, does there exist a term having the type in the given dimension? A key result of [7] is that the dimension-bounded inhabitation problem is undecidable in set-theoretic dimension ([7], Theorem 28) but decidable and EXPSPACE-complete in multiset dimension ([7], Theorem 34). For any fixed dimensional parameter, the latter problem is PSPACE-complete. The main previous result concerning decidable fragments of the inhabitation problem for intersection types had been given by Urzyczyn [19], showing that the problem is decidable and EXPSPACE-complete in rank 2, and undecidable in all ranks k for k ≥ 3 (here referring to Leivant’s notion of rank [13]). All rank 2 typings are derivable in linear multiset dimension [7, Proposition 23] (meaning dimension n for an intersection type with n components). Therefore, bounded multiset dimension strictly generalizes the rank 2 borderline: typings in bounded multiset dimension span all ranks. In this paper we introduce and study a system (denoted system R1 ) with bounded parallel intersection providing a strict generalization of the multiset dimensional system [7], extending (and deepening the analysis of) decidable inhabitation under dimensional bound. Intuitively, system R occupies a position between the set-theoretic and the multiset dimensional systems of [7], employing a combination of intersection types represented as vectors of types (which are non-idempotent) and as sets of types (which are idempotent). A technical novelty of the system is the use of relations specifying type vector transformations that, intuitively, capture information flow between types in a derivation, and which mediate between vectors of types and sets of types. Dimensionality in this system is measured by the maximal length of vectors of sets of types that can be used to type a variable. Our main technical result is that inhabitation in bounded dimension is decidable in 2-EXPTIME, and for each fixed dimension, inhabitation is decidable in EXPTIME. We have corresponding lower bounds of EXPSPACE and PSPACE, respectively, and leave open the problem of closing the gaps. 1 The name system R has been used by de Carvalho [6] for a different system; we refer to his system as system Rel, where relations play a major role in its denotational semantics. Related work. There are several intersection type systems with features that partially overlap with those of system R. However, none of these systems combines a syntax-directed Curry-style presentation with concise information flow management.
